title: 3 things AI quietly eroded in my engineering team

scenes.narration: Leadership expected AI to make us several times faster. We tried to build an AI factory, but our velocity barely increased, and I burned out.
Mid-year, I started analysing why we couldn't ship faster. And I noticed something deeper: how AI was quietly changing our work and our team.
First, the cost of building. It forced us to choose. Now every idea comes as a demo. Code was never the bottleneck. Deciding is.
Second, the ladder of experience. With AI, juniors sound sure. Seniors still say: it depends. Guess who gets heard, and who fixes it later.
Third, asking each other for help. Now we ask a chatbot. Faster, yes. But those questions made people feel needed, and brought us closer.
None of this shows up in a sprint report. It used to come for free. Now it has to be built on purpose.
I'm still positive about AI, but it's hard to adapt to what you haven't noticed. Read the full, much deeper story on my blog.
